model_organism.citation: Kim et al. 2019 - Vascular defects of DYRK1A knockouts are ameliorated by modulating calcium signaling in zebrafish (PMID: 31043432)
phenotypes: dyrk1aa mutant embryos showed cerebral hemorrhage
defective angiogenesis of central arteries in the developing hindbrain
phenotypes rescued by wild-type dyrk1aa mRNA but not kinase-dead mRNA, showing kinase activity is required
hemorrhage rescued by the calcium chelator EGTA and by FK506 (calcium signaling modulation)
transcriptomic analysis showed altered calcium signaling networks

model_organism.citation: Dyrk1a haploinsufficiency study - DYRK1A promotes dopaminergic neuron survival in the developing brain and in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease (PMID: 24922073)
phenotypes: mesencephalic dopaminergic neurons generated at normal rates in the embryo
reduced number of mDA neurons postnatally in Dyrk1a+/- mice, caused by abnormal Casp9-dependent apoptosis during the main wave of programmed cell death
Dyrk1a phosphorylation of Casp9 at Thr125 restrains apoptosis
mBACtgDyrk1a (3 copies) mice showed increased mDA cell number and attenuated MPTP-induced loss of SN dopaminergic neurons

model_organism.citation: Overexpression of Dyrk1A is implicated in several cognitive, electrophysiological and neuromorphological alterations found in a mouse model of Down syndrome (PMID: 25188425)
phenotypes: Dyrk1a+/- was crossed onto Ts65Dn to normalize Dyrk1a copy number from 3 to 2
improved working and reference memory in the Morris water maze
restored adult dentate gyrus cell proliferation and differentiation
restored GABAergic and glutamatergic synaptic marker density
no effect on hyperactivity/attention, DG volume or granule cell density

biological.citation: Li et al. 2015 - Integrative Analysis of Human Protein Complexes Reveals Biochemical Activities and Convergent Mechanisms of Action in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASHG 2015)
biological.summary: Mass spectrometry in neuronal culture purified and identified proteins co-complexed with DYRK1A, alongside ANK2, CHD8, CUL3 and POGZ. The interactors form an ASD-relevant network that is preferentially expressed in early fetal brain and regulated by FMRP and MeCP2.

biological.citation: Walter et al. 2021 - Global kinome profiling reveals DYRK1A as critical activator of the human mitochondrial import machinery (PMID: 34257281)
biological.summary: DYRK1A phosphorylates the mitochondrial import receptor TOM70 at Ser91, which promotes TOM70 interaction with the TOM core translocase and activates carrier protein import. DYRK1A inhibition impairs mitochondrial structure and function and triggers a protective transcriptional response.

biological.citation: Downregulated Wnt/β-catenin signalling in the Down syndrome hippocampus (PMID: 31086297)
biological.summary: Wnt/β-catenin signalling is downregulated in the hippocampus of adults with DS and Alzheimer's disease and in the Tc1 mouse. DYRK1A regulates Wnt bimodally: it is a negative regulator under basal conditions and enhances signalling after pathway activation.

biological.citation: Modulation of the Wnt pathway through inhibition of CLK2 and DYRK1A by lorecivivint (PMID: 31132406)
biological.summary: Lorecivivint inhibits DYRK1A-mediated phosphorylation of SIRT1 and FOXO1. DYRK1A siRNA knockdown in hMSCs and BEAS-2B cells modulated Wnt targets and enhanced mature chondrocyte function. Knockdown alone was sufficient for anti-inflammatory effects (NF-κB/STAT3 reduction).

biological.citation: Embryonic organizer formation disorder leads to multiorgan dysplasia in Down syndrome (PMID: 36535930)
biological.summary: Overexpressing human DYRK1A in zebrafish impaired the embryonic organizer and body axis, giving DS-like nervous, heart, visceral and blood abnormalities. Phosphoproteomics showed anomalous phosphorylation of β-catenin and Hsp90ab1, enhancing Wnt and inhibiting TGF-β signalling. Rebalancing Wnt/TGF-β rescued abnormal proliferation of DS HSCs.

biological.citation: Increased dosage of DYRK1A leads to congenital heart defects in a mouse model of Down syndrome (PMID: 38266108)
biological.summary: Genetic mapping in Dp1Tyb mice showed that a third copy of Dyrk1a causes congenital heart defects. Reducing Dyrk1a from three copies to two restored cardiomyocyte proliferation and mitochondrial respiration and rescued septation defects. Fetal DS hearts and Dp1Tyb embryonic hearts both showed reduced expression of mitochondrial respiration and proliferation genes.

biological.citation: DYRK1A enhances antitumor immunity in type 1 conventional dendritic cells via mTORC1 activation (PMID: 42024470)
biological.summary: DYRK1A responds to TLR and growth factor stimulation and phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser540, causing TSC2 degradation and activating mTORC1 in cDC1s. Dyrk1a ablation in cDC1s impaired antitumor immunity, and Tsc2 deletion rescued it.

biological.citation: An inhibitory circuit-based enhancer of DYRK1A function reverses Dyrk1a-associated impairment in social recognition (PMID: 37797581)
biological.summary: In heterozygous Dyrk1a mice, DYRK1A supports mossy fiber–PV interneuron feedforward inhibition of CA3/CA2 for social recognition. The cytoskeletal protein ABLIM3 was identified as a synaptic substrate. Ablim3 downregulation or chemogenetic PV IN activation rescued social recognition.

biological.citation: DYRK1A is a multifunctional host factor that regulates coronavirus replication in a kinase-independent manner (PMID: 38099687)
biological.summary: A CRISPR screen and knockout showed DYRK1A, but not DYRK1B, is required for TGEV replication through a kinase-independent, nuclear-dependent mechanism. DYRK1A loss reduced expression of the receptor ANPEP, inhibited viral entry and impaired double-membrane vesicle formation. It is also proviral for MHV, PDCoV and PSV.

biological.citation: Impaired macroglial development and axonal conductivity contributes to the neuropathology of DYRK1A-related intellectual disability syndrome (PMID: 36402907)
biological.summary: Dyrk1a+/- mice show increased cortical astrogliogenesis and delayed oligodendrocyte lineage progression. They also have fewer, thinner myelinated callosal axons with abnormal nodes of Ranvier and slower action potential conduction.
